title: Retention devices and calls to action
purpose: Finds the devices that keep viewers watching (open loops, countdowns, re-hooks, pattern interrupts) and the call to action, with placement as ratios of runtime.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F4 contact sheet; F1 at each claimed device; the last 5 s frame by frame (F8) for the CTA.
pitfalls: Claiming a device works (retention effect) when only its presence is observable
Calling every cut a pattern interrupt

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F4: Whole-video contact sheet, 1 frame per second: ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=1,scale=180:-2,tile=8x8" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/sheet.jpg" (or use the keyframes and contact sheet from video_re_keyframes_contact_sheet)
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.F10: Similarity of two frames (SSIM, 1.0 = identical): ffmpeg -i a.jpg -i b.jpg -lavfi "[0:v]scale=320:-2[a];[1:v]scale=320:-2[b];[a][b]ssim" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"
recipes.A3: Momentary loudness every 100 ms (LUFS): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -af "ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.M:file=$WORK/lufs_m.txt" -f null -

questions.question: Which retention devices are present (open loop, countdown or ordinal progress, re-hook, pattern interrupt, teaser, cliffhanger, payoff promise), each with timestamps?
questions.how_to_answer: Combine label sequences (text_regions), caption phrasing (analysis only), visual interrupts (F4) and audio hits; list each device with timestamps.
questions.challenge: Presence is observable, effect is not: reject any claim that a device 'increases retention'.

questions.question: How many open loops are opened, and when is each closed?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes open-loop rules with open and close ratios.
questions.how_to_answer: Find statements that withhold information and the later resolution; give both times as ratios.
questions.challenge: Each loop must have a resolution time or be marked unresolved.

questions.question: Does the viewer see progress through the list (ordinal labels, countdown numbers, 'N of M')?
questions.how_to_answer: Label crops (F3) per item.
questions.challenge: Progress bars count too; say which form.

questions.question: Is there a mid-video re-hook (a new promise or teaser in the middle), and at what ratio?
questions.how_to_answer: Look between 35% and 65% of runtime for a teaser of what is coming.
questions.challenge: A plain transition to the next item is not a re-hook.

questions.question: Is there a call to action, and what kind (follow, comment, share, save, watch part 2, link)?
questions.how_to_answer: Check the last 15% of captions and text crops.
questions.challenge: Spoken-only CTAs are easy to miss; check the audio transcript too.

questions.question: At what fraction of the runtime does the CTA start (seconds before the end in the note)?
questions.how_to_answer: First CTA cue time / duration; duration - time.
questions.challenge: Report both values.

questions.question: Is the CTA spoken, shown on screen, or both?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare captions and text crops at the CTA time.
questions.challenge: Check both channels.

questions.question: How long does the CTA last?
questions.how_to_answer: From first to last CTA cue.
questions.challenge: Recompute.

questions.question: Does the video ask a specific question to prompt comments?
questions.how_to_answer: Questions in the last 20% of captions or text.
questions.challenge: Rhetorical questions answered in the video do not count.

questions.question: Is the video framed as part of a series (part numbers, 'next episode' tease)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds series fields to the format.
questions.how_to_answer: Text crops and captions at the start and end.
questions.challenge: The series name must not be carried into the format.

questions.question: Does the last line or frame lead back into the first (seamless loop for rewatching)?
questions.how_to_answer: F10 between the last and first frames; compare the last caption's structure with the hook's (analysis only).
questions.challenge: Visual similarity alone (same template) is not a loop; the sentence must continue too.

questions.question: Are visual progress indicators used (progress bar, dots, timeline)?
questions.why_it_matters: Records presence; some house styles forbid them, so the IR must say.
questions.how_to_answer: F1 frames at 25%, 50%, 75% of runtime.
questions.challenge: Check all three frames.

questions.question: How many reasons to keep watching are stated in the hook (for example 'number 1 will surprise you', 'stay for the last one')?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the count of hook promises.
questions.how_to_answer: Count promise statements in the first 10% (captions, analysis only).
questions.challenge: The topic statement itself is not a promise.

questions.question: Is the best item explicitly teased as saved for last?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a 'best last' ordering rule with a tease.
questions.how_to_answer: Captions in the first half referencing the final item.
questions.challenge: Give the timestamp of the tease.

questions.question: Are there interaction prompts mid-video (pause to guess, comment your answer, look closely)?
questions.how_to_answer: Captions and text crops in the middle 60%.
questions.challenge: List each prompt.

questions.question: How many seconds pass between the payoff and the end of the video?
questions.how_to_answer: duration - payoff beat end (from structure).
questions.challenge: Cross-check with the structure lens.

questions.question: How is the CTA drawn on screen (text only, button shape, arrow pointing at UI, animated icon)?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 at the CTA.
questions.challenge: Platform-native UI is not part of the video.

questions.question: What is the median time between new-information moments (new fact, new number, new visual)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a 'new information every N seconds' rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Merge times of new labels, new key numbers and new assets; median gap.
questions.challenge: New captions repeating the same idea are not new information.

questions.question: Which pattern interrupts occur (sudden zoom, sound hit, colour flash, layout change, silence), with timestamps?
questions.why_it_matters: Lists interrupt devices for the generator.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine transitions, effects and audio drops; list with type.
questions.challenge: Ordinary cuts are not interrupts; each must break the established pattern.

questions.question: Is there a mid-video cliffhanger (an unresolved moment right before a section change)?
questions.how_to_answer: Captions near section ends with an unresolved question or reveal held across the boundary.
questions.challenge: The resolution must come after the boundary.

questions.question: How often is the viewer addressed directly on screen (text containing 'you' or an imperative)?
questions.how_to_answer: Count text crops with direct address / minute.
questions.challenge: Report the count and duration.

questions.question: Is the benefit to the viewer stated early (what they will learn or get), and when?
questions.how_to_answer: Captions in the first 15% with a benefit statement.
questions.challenge: Give the timestamp; topic mention is not a benefit.

questions.question: Are social proof cues used (counts of people, expert references, results achieved)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds proof slots that require sourced numbers in variants.
questions.how_to_answer: Captions and text crops with numbers about people or authority.
questions.challenge: Every proof cue becomes a claim that needs a source in a variant.

questions.question: Write the retention placement rule (re-hook ratio, CTA ratio, interrupt interval) in terms of parameters.
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler procedural retention placement.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine 004, 006 and 019, for example 're-hook at 0.45-0.55; CTA starts at duration - cta_s; interrupt every 8-12 s'.
questions.challenge: Re-derive the source's device times from the rule.

questions.question: Which retention parameters should a new video set (cta_kind, cta_text slot, rehook_at_ratio, open_loop)?
questions.how_to_answer: Collect 004, 005, 006 and 002.
questions.challenge: Each parameter needs derived_from.

questions.question: Does the CTA come before the payoff (interrupting content) or after it?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare CTA time with the payoff beat.
questions.challenge: Cross-check with structure_beats-016.

questions.question: Which frames would work as thumbnails (clear subject, readable text, high contrast)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a thumbnail selection rule for the rendered variant.
questions.how_to_answer: Pick 3 frames from F4 that meet the criteria; give timestamps and the measured text size and contrast.
questions.challenge: Thumbnails are never exported from the source; the rule applies to the variant.

questions.question: Which stretches have no new visual or verbal information for more than 4 seconds?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a negative rule (avoid dead stretches) with measured examples.
questions.how_to_answer: Gaps in the merged event list (new text, new asset, new sentence) longer than 4 s.
questions.challenge: Report the event sources merged.

questions.question: Does the number of items delivered match the number promised in the hook?
questions.why_it_matters: A consistency rule for generated scripts.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare the hook's promised count (title or captions) with n_items.
questions.challenge: If no count was promised, answer not determinable.

questions.question: Is there an end card with additional prompts (next video, subscribe graphic), and how long?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 over the last 3 s.
questions.challenge: Cross-check with structure_beats-010.
